summary.title: Threagile - Agile Threat Modeling Toolkit
summary.one_liner: Threagile is an open-source toolkit that lets you model an architecture as a YAML file, run risk-rule checks against it, and generate risk reports with mitigation advice and data-flow diagrams.
takeaways: Threagile models an architecture and its assets declaratively in a YAML file that can be edited in an IDE or any YAML editor.
Running the toolkit applies risk rules to the model and produces a report of potential risks with mitigation advice.
It automatically creates data-flow diagrams and outputs in Excel and JSON formats.
Risk tracking can be kept inside the YAML model so the current mitigation state is reported.
It can run from the command line, as a Docker container, or as a REST server.
summary.summary: The Threagile homepage presents an open-source toolkit for Agile Threat Modeling, aimed at fitting into DevSecOps workflows. Teams describe their architecture and assets in a YAML model file, and the toolkit runs a set of risk rules against that model. Output includes a risk report with mitigation advice, automatically generated data-flow diagrams, and Excel and JSON exports. Risk tracking can also be recorded in the YAML file. The page notes it can be run via CLI, Docker, or as a REST server, and that it was released at Black Hat Arsenal 2020 and DEF CON 2020 AppSec Village. The page is brief and does not go into detailed setup steps.
